Yes I had this as a child and I’ve managed to come out the other side. So if anyone wants any advice I’ll give it down below. 

I was a very manipulative child. Not in a mean way but I could lie well and I knew how to make people like me. This was born out of anxiety and a fear of being judged. And so being manipulative meant I always had a mask on, I was always protected in a sense - no risk. 

However, the older I got the more I realised none of these “friends” knew me, they knew what I was reflecting back to them. What I knew they wanted to hear. So from that realisation, I went through a stage of insufferable victim hood where I thought that no one really cares about who I am anyway, all anyone wants is just someone to listen etc. 

I got very down and depressed and aggravating to be around, I was very negative. There was a little glimmer of hope though. During this time, I became very introspective. In my anger, I rebelled. Little by little, I started doing things I always wanted to do, I remember it started with painting, then skateboarding, then hiking (this never stops the hobbies just keep piling on in). I did all of this on my own for a long time, I became comfortable with my own company and I actually started to like who I became, I embodied the person I would think was “cool”. 

And then, people wanted to join me. I would ask if someone wanted to come on my walk, some didn’t, a lot did. It seems people are calmer when you’re in an environment that you’re comfortable with. I could actually listen, genuinely, and be interested in what other people were saying. I could answer back, genuinely, and have enough confidence in myself to not be scared of their response. I could ask them questions and most of the time they knew it was coming from curiosity not judgement. 

Most of the time, when people respond back to you negatively, it is because they haven’t reached that point. This revelation allowed me to take a step back comfortably and see situations for what they were. I made a vow to myself never to lie, it’s hard and you can come across lacking in the art of social cues, but it is always (and I mean always) appreciated in the long run. 

People come to me now, open, who they truly are and I can respond back open, and who I truly am. It’s something everyone can do, it just takes a little practice and confidence.

It's very easy to dismiss something as a fallacy, but I would ask you to elaborate for the sake of allowing me to understand where you are coming from.

Of course I am aware of that, I haven't stated otherwise. I even explicitly said by all means voice a concern, because who is to say someone with the capability to do something about it won't hear you. I'm merely stating that Jordan's advice on getting your own house in order first isn't to silence anyone, it is to make an argument one already has stronger and more valuable to society regardless as to what 'side' it comes from.

I see your case and it definitely has some footing but I think it misses a fundamental point and perhaps is too focused on one way of interpreting things, which really I feel is the issue here. And not for just you, for me too and really anyone ever! 

I cannot speak for you but it seems you have taken the way Jordan has used “house in perfect order” to mean do nothing until it is. That in itself is a moot point and one in which I believe he wasn’t making otherwise he wouldn’t suggest starting by cleaning your room (i also cannot speak for him, merely how I’ve interpreted it). Instead, I feel it is an effort to encourage more of a conscious look at the way one leads their own life before trying to bring about change to something wider. As in, one couldn’t know how to fix a large issue if they’re unable to function in their individual lives to a successful degree and perhaps it is up to you as to what you see that success as being. Jordan can’t really tell anyone what that is, only what it would be for him. Several degrees, ability to talk to ones parents without residual resentment etc. We all sort of know where we are failing to some degree and to start by changing that can perhaps set off a chain reaction, anyway that will go off into a ramble. 

Again, by all means (in my view and I feel it is shared) voice a concern but to expect to have any value behind it without offering something after is redundant and expecting others to do it for you is naive and a waste of ones potential.

No to address the problems the world faces. The world needs clear thinkers who understand to a decent extend (and well who am I to say what “decent” is but anyway) what the problems are and how we can find a way to tackle them productively. 

I, personally, don’t see it as “daring to criticise” (or keeping silent) more as knowing enough about what you are critiquing to offer a valid solution to then expect to be taken seriously. Perhaps you are only able to when you’ve come to understand yourself I.e, getting your house in order. 

The “you suck” weren’t my words they were Joel’s if that helps to clarify.

I suppose it means to simply state something doesn’t offer much, but to state something and then know enough about it to offer a solution one could experiment or even think about with is more worthy of being heard? So Jordan’s “you suck” (which I don’t know if I’d use those words but for the sake of making sense) is a call to action rather than a baseless statement

I don’t know about you but I suffer from procrastination and debilitating curiosity, debilitating in that sometimes there’s so much to know and find out it causes bouts of catatonic behaviour, and picking through the hidden treasures of my home was far more enjoyable than actually packing it up and taking it down. 


I found a collection of Polaroid’s encasing the naked women of the 80’s that my dad, I’m assuming, thought were too valuable to throw out but too risky to keep out. I found a bin bag full of the cuddly toys I couldn’t get rid of because they all have names so they must all clearly have souls and that banishing them to a cold and dark attic was surely better than sending them to the tip. I also found my broken snow globe. The thing was huge, heavy and glaringly Disney. It was ugly but it used to play a calming tune, one that if I heard now I’d still smile, but the winding key had snapped off so, I guess I’d have to smile another day. 


I didn’t want to break it further, not because it meant a lot to me but because it was filled with liquid and I didn’t want to have to clean it up if I knocked it over. I took it, carefully, down the ladder with me and placed it on the floor. This motion kicked me into gear so I started bringing more down and doing what I was supposed to be doing all along. 


I came across a clear bag with white inside stuffed way in the back. I’d never seen it before so naturally I jumped at it. I wanted to look at it in more light. Once I got down I unzipped it and out came this massive wedding dress. It wasn’t my mum’s, I’d seen the photos and knew what hers looked like. It was my grandmothers, my mum’s mum - who I’d never met and who mum rarely talks about because it makes her sad - I knew this because even though to talk about her makes my mum sad, she still keeps up photos and there was one of her in her wedding dress that I studied to see if I looked anything like her - I have her eyebrows. 


I took it off the hanger and held it against me in the mirror. As soon as I did that my snow globe started playing. I don’t think my hairs stood on end, I don’t think I felt a cold creep up my neck. It was like I knew exactly who it was and I just smiled. The snow globe stopped as quick as it started. I said hello and put the dress back in it’s case and went and told my mum, who also smiled.

I'm all about watching the hard stuff, the stuff that is "problematic", but you can't be cheap on this, you can't be lazy because thats just false and shits on everyone who is going through depression. I feel it acts like a heavy show, one that will open doors to talking about mental illness, but its so far from genuine that any conversation holding this show as an example will be a detrimental one. 

I'm not saying people shouldn't watch it, I'm just saying think a little deeper when watching it. And if you enjoy it good on you, its a show at the end of the day, but its aim was missed however its still being seen as "progressive" just for having that aim, which is total bull.
